# A strict-quota product profile with an exact full-cone martingale obstruction

This note proves a bounded auxiliary obstruction on an actual complete lattice base. The previously separate global-criticality obligation is now proved by the exact all-normal certificate in `candidate de93c4f08837e128`. The canonical caps attain the true global depth; this conclusion uses that full certificate, not section-centroid stationarity.

## 1. The actual product and its canonical profile

In integer dimension two set

    D4=conv{(-4,-4),(4,0),(0,4)}, P=D4 intersect Z^2,
    ell0(z)=-z1-z2, ell1(z)=2z1-z2, ell2(z)=2z2-z1.

Thus `P={z in Z^2:ell_j(z)>=-4 for all j}`. It has 31 points, with parity class sizes `10,7,7,7`; the even-even class has size ten and contains all three outer vertices.

Let `K` be any full-dimensional triangle with barycentric coordinates `lambda0,lambda1,lambda2`, area `V`, and centroid `g`. The convex body `C=D4 times K` has exactly the 31 equal positive fibers. Define

    H_j={lambda_j(x)-1/3+ell_j(z)>=0},
    W=(1/3) sum_j 1_Hj, eta=sum_z H_1|boundary K_z.

For each `j`, exactly twelve bases have `ell_j>0`, three have `ell_j=0`, and sixteen have `ell_j<0`. Since these offsets are integers, the positive traces are strictly full, the negative ones strictly empty, and the zero traces are canonical centroid caps. Consequently every cap has raw mass

    Q=(12+3(4/9))V=(40/3)V, M=31V, beta=Q/M=40/93.   (1)

Their margins sum identically to zero, so the caps cover the ambient space and prove the true global depth is at most `Q`.

Every cap's three proper sections have the same continuous centroid `g`. The three bases on its zero slice sum to zero, so its full mixed section centroid is `(0,g)`. The total coarea masses agree by the vertex-permutation symmetry of `D4`, giving the displayed equal response weights. All other traces are strictly separated from the cap boundaries. Thus these are proper, regular, common-mass stationary cap data. The independent all-normal certificate proves global attainment of (1).

## 2. All strict proper-closed-minor count quotas hold

Call `T subset P` closed when `P intersect conv(T)=T`, and let `k(T)` be its number of parity classes. Every nonempty proper closed set satisfies

    |T|/31 < k(T)/4,                                (2)

indeed with margin at least `1/124`.

First, a closed set containing two distinct points contains the entire primitive lattice segment between them, and hence at least two parities. Therefore `k(T)=1` forces `|T|=1`.

Second, a two-dimensional complete lattice-convex set contains a unimodular triangle, hence at least three parity classes. Here is an elementary proof of the first assertion. Choose a lattice triangle of least positive area among the points of the set. If its determinant had absolute value at least two, a nonzero lattice coset in its half-open edge parallelogram would give a lattice point `p=alpha v+beta w`, `0<=alpha,beta<1`, distinct from the three vertices. Either `alpha+beta<=1`, so `p` lies in the triangle, or `v+w-p` does. Closure puts this new point in the set and subdivision gives a smaller positive-area triangle, a contradiction. The resulting determinant-one triangle has three distinct parities because its two edge vectors are linearly independent modulo two.

Thus `k(T)=2` forces a collinear set. The whole base lies in `[-4,4]^2`; a primitive lattice line has a nonzero integer coordinate step, so it contains at most nine points there. Hence `|T|<=9`.

If `k(T)=3` and the missing class is even-even, then `|T|<=21`. If another seven-point class is missing, closure prevents `T` from containing all three even outer vertices, since those vertices span `D4`. At least one more point is therefore omitted, giving `|T|<=23`. Finally `k(T)=4` and properness give `|T|<=30`.

The four bounds imply

    1/4-1/31=27/124,
    1/2-9/31=13/62,
    3/4-23/31=1/124,
    1-30/31=1/31.

This proves (2) without enumerating the exponentially many point subsets. The fibers have equal positive areas, so (2) is exactly the strict normalized mass quota for this product family. It is not the stronger quantitative inequality involving an as-yet-unknown bad depth `beta/ Gamma_2`.

## 3. The full convex-potential optimum is beta, not Gamma_2

Consider any finite nonnegative normal-dependent potential `Phi(n,z,x)` convex in the physical variables `(z,x)` for every fixed normal and having finite positive denominator. We prove

    integral Phi W d eta <= (40/93) integral Phi d eta.   (3)

The constant potential attains equality. Thus the supremum over this entire cone is exactly `40/93`, with strict gap

    4/9-40/93=4/279.                                (4)

It is enough to prove (3) separately on each continuous facet, because its normal is fixed. Relabeling barycentric coordinates and simultaneously permuting the base simplex vertices takes one facet to any other; the corresponding base map is unimodular, since it sends the integer basis vertices to integer vertices and its inverse does the same. Surface length changes by a constant on a facet, which cancels from the inequality. We may therefore use facet `lambda0=0`, parametrized by

    lambda1=t, lambda2=1-t, 0<=t<=1.

For each base `z`, split this interval into thirds by writing

    t=(r+s)/3, 0<r<1, s in {0,1,2}.

Ignoring only the finitely many interval endpoints of surface measure zero, the value `3W` at `(z,t)` is the integer

    w(z,s)=number{j:ell_j(z)>0}
           +1_{ell1(z)=0, s>=1}
           +1_{ell2(z)=0, s<=1}.                    (5)

It is always one or two. Among the 93 points `(z,s)`, exactly 27 have value two and 66 have value one. Denote these lists by `H` and `L` respectively, in lexicographic `(z1,z2,s)` order.

### Exact martingale certificate

The file `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/r4_facet_martingale_exact_slab_recovery.json` gives 144 strictly positive rational numbers `pi_hl`, all other entries being zero, satisfying exactly

    sum_l pi_hl=22              for every h in H,
    sum_h pi_hl=9               for every l in L,
    sum_l pi_hl l=22 h          for every h in H.     (6)

All three coordinates are preserved in the final equation. The JSON records the complete integer point lists and every numerator and denominator, so (6) is a finite explicit rational certificate rather than an assertion of numerical feasibility. Its common denominator divides `4,418,652`. The standalone verifier `../assets/pk-nov6/computations/verify_r4_facet_martingale_slab_recovery.py` checks positivity, both marginals, and every coordinate identity using only integer/Fraction arithmetic, without a numerical solver. It passes 732 exact checks, including the additional geometric and quota arithmetic in this note.

For each fixed `r`, the affine map

    (z,s) -> (z,(r+s)/3)

preserves (6). Convexity and Jensen's inequality therefore give

    22 sum_(h in H) Phi(n,z_h,x((r+s_h)/3))
       <=9 sum_(l in L) Phi(n,z_l,x((r+s_l)/3)).       (7)

Integrate in `r` and use `dt=dr/3`. Since `beta-1/3=9/93` and `2/3-beta=22/93`, equation (7) is exactly (3) on the chosen facet. The same proof applies to the other facets. This proves the full-cone upper bound.

For the constant potential, each facet has the same normalized profile integral

    sum_z integral_0^1 W(z,t) dt
      =[2(27)+66]/9=40/3.

Its normalized denominator is 31. Therefore equality in (3) is attained.

The exploratory linear program was used only to locate a support. It is not invoked in this proof: (6), checked as exact rational identities, is the complete finite certificate used by Jensen.

## 4. Exposed edges also fail, with an exact smaller optimum

For example, on the exposed base edge `z1+z2=4`, the five integer bases are `(r,4-r)`, `0<=r<=4`. None of their three offsets vanishes. Their profiles are constant throughout the whole continuous body, with values

    (1/3,1/3,2/3,1/3,1/3).

For any nonnegative convex potential, its integral over the continuous boundary at those five bases is a nonnegative convex sequence `f_0,...,f_4`. Convexity gives `f_0+f_4>=2f_2` and `f_1+f_3>=2f_2`, hence `sum f_r>=5f_2`. Its edge efficiency is at most

    1/3+(1/3) f_2/(sum f_r)<=2/5.

A constant potential attains `2/5`. The exposed-face localization lemma transfers such local tests to the full family, but cannot increase this exact local optimum. The other two edges are equivalent by symmetry.

For comparison, the tentative dilation-three edge computation must retain its two zero offsets: their extra traces are canonical partial caps, rather than full fibers. On the continuous facet opposite the missing cap their mean profiles are `5/9`, giving the edge constant value exactly `4/9`, not `1/2`.

## 5. The true global center is already known

The point `(0,g)` is a global deepest point of this actual product. There is also a symmetry proof of its maximizing property which does not require the independent exact calculation of its depth (1). To see this, define raw halfspace depth at every point of the full ambient space. Its upper level sets are convex: a halfspace containing a convex combination of points contains at least one of those points, and hence has mass at least their minimum depth.

Depth is invariant under the independent finite groups permuting the three base vertices and the three continuous vertices. These maps preserve the actual lattice set `P`, preserve uniform area on `K`, and map ambient halfspaces to ambient halfspaces. Averaging the full finite orbit of any point of `S` gives precisely `(0,g)`. Convexity of depth regions therefore makes its depth at least that of the original point. This average belongs to the actual set, since `0 in P` and `g in K`.

This is a valid center argument in the product family; it is not an attempt to replace a missing mixed point by an arbitrary average.

## 6. Global criticality is now independently certified; the remaining scope

The exact finite proof in
`candidate de93c4f08837e128`
proves

    every closed ambient halfspace through (0,g)
    captures at least (40/3)V.                       (8)

Its proof covers all oblique normals, repeated continuous heights, and
pure-base closed halfspaces including their boundary-fiber mass. The
standalone independent verifier checks 525,779 exact identities and
inequalities, including 11,188 nonnegative cubic leaves and 3,911
subdivisions with full coverage. A second independent implementation and
root audit agree. This establishes that the displayed caps are genuinely
globally critical. The common cap masses, full section centroids and
symmetries alone were never substituted for this lower bound.

Consequently the strict count quotas, actual lattice completeness,
regular global criticality and convex compatibility together do not imply
individual Gamma_2 potential efficiency: its exact optimum here is
40/93<4/9. The normalized depth 40/93 is nevertheless far above the OC
target 1/9. This does not refute an individual-efficiency statement with
the additional bad-depth hypothesis beta<Gamma_2/4, nor OC itself.
Moreover the attained-minimum quantitative quotas involving the numerical
depth parameter remain stronger premises than these count inequalities;
they must not be silently substituted for one another.
